name: Indonesia
summary: Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK) licenses and supervises conventional commercial banks, sets their AML/CFT/CPF, governance, conduct, IT and staff-development rules, and supervises market conduct under the 2023 P2SK Law. Bank Indonesia runs monetary and payment-system policy and protects consumers in the activities it supervises. PPATK is the financial intelligence unit. Training duties are explicit: POJK 8/2023 requires AML/CFT/CPF training at least yearly, POJK 22/2023 sets consumer protection training, POJK 12/2024 yearly anti-fraud education, and OJK rules require risk management certificates for boards and key officers and a minimum staff-development budget.

regulators.name: Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (Financial Services Authority)
regulators.role: Integrated financial regulator; licenses and supervises banks and issues binding regulations (POJK) and circulars on AML/CFT/CPF, governance, consumer protection, IT and cyber risk, anti-fraud and staff certification.

regulators.name: Bank Indonesia
regulators.role: Central bank responsible for monetary, macroprudential and payment-system policy; issues consumer protection rules for the payment and other activities it supervises.

regulators.name: Pusat Pelaporan dan Analisis Transaksi Keuangan (Indonesian Financial Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre)
regulators.role: Indonesia's financial intelligence unit; receives suspicious, cash and cross-border transfer reports from banks and publishes reporting guidance and the terrorist list mechanism.

regulators.name: Direktorat Jenderal Pajak (Directorate General of Taxes)
regulators.role: Indonesian tax authority that receives financial account information reported by banks for automatic exchange with partner jurisdictions (FATCA and CRS).

programs.title: Indonesia | APU PPT Programme Awareness under POJK 8/2023
programs.why: POJK 8/2023 makes human resources and training one of the five pillars of a bank's AML/CFT/CPF programme and requires training for officers and staff at least annually, with directors accountable for making sure new joiners and relevant units attend. Staff also need to understand Law 8/2010, which defines money laundering, sets reporting duties and bars tipping off.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Banks must train officers and staff on AML, CFT and CPF at least once a year, more often where risk or major changes call for it; content covers the laws, ML/TF/PF typologies, internal policies and each employee's role, and training must be evaluated.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Directors must ensure officers and staff, particularly those in relevant units and new joiners, attend AML/CFT/CPF training once a year.

references.title: Undang-Undang Nomor 8 Tahun 2010 tentang Pencegahan dan Pemberantasan Tindak Pidana Pencucian Uang (Law 8/2010 on the Prevention and Eradication of Money Laundering)
references.issuer: Republic of Indonesia (copy published by OJK)
references.note: Reporting parties must report suspicious, large cash and cross-border transfer transactions to PPATK, suspicious ones within three working days; staff may not tell the customer about a report.

programs.title: Indonesia | Countering Terrorism Financing (UU TPPT and POJK 8/2023)
programs.why: The annual training required by POJK 8/2023 covers terrorism financing alongside money laundering. Law 9/2013 adds its own duties: suspicious transactions linked to terrorism financing go to PPATK within three working days, tipping off is a crime, and funds of listed persons must be frozen immediately.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Banks must train officers and staff on AML, CFT and CPF at least once a year, more often where risk or major changes call for it; content covers the laws, ML/TF/PF typologies, internal policies and each employee's role, and training must be evaluated.

references.title: Undang-Undang Nomor 9 Tahun 2013 tentang Pencegahan dan Pemberantasan Tindak Pidana Pendanaan Terorisme (Law 9/2013 on the Prevention and Eradication of Terrorism Financing)
references.issuer: Republic of Indonesia (copy published by OJK)
references.note: Financial service providers must report TF-related suspicious transactions to PPATK within three working days, must not disclose such reports, and must freeze immediately the funds of persons on the court-confirmed terrorist list.

programs.title: Indonesia | Countering Proliferation Financing (PPPSPM)
programs.why: POJK 8/2023 extended Indonesia's AML/CFT programme to the financing of weapons of mass destruction. The mandatory annual training must cover PPPSPM rules and typologies, and banks must maintain the proliferation-financing list (DPPSPM) supplied through OJK and screen customers against it.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Banks must train officers and staff on AML, CFT and CPF at least once a year, more often where risk or major changes call for it; content covers the laws, ML/TF/PF typologies, internal policies and each employee's role, and training must be evaluated.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Banks must keep the DTTOT and DPPSPM lists up to date through the OJK system, must not make funds available to listed persons, and must match customers against the lists while managing false positives and negatives.

programs.title: Indonesia | Customer Due Diligence under POJK 8/2023
programs.why: POJK 8/2023 sets when CDD is mandatory (new relationships, transactions of IDR 100 million or more, fund transfers, suspicion, doubtful information) and what must be identified and verified. Law 8/2010 requires reporting parties to apply know-your-customer principles. The rules impose duties on the bank rather than a separate course, but the annual AML training must explain these procedures.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: CDD is required at onboarding, for transactions of at least IDR 100 million, for fund transfers, on suspicion or when information is doubtful; anonymous or fictitious-name accounts are prohibited.

references.title: Undang-Undang Nomor 8 Tahun 2010 tentang Pencegahan dan Pemberantasan Tindak Pidana Pencucian Uang (Law 8/2010 on the Prevention and Eradication of Money Laundering)
references.issuer: Republic of Indonesia (copy published by OJK)
references.note: Reporting parties must apply the know-your-customer principle set by their supervisor and must end the relationship, and report it as suspicious, where a customer refuses KYC or gives doubtful information.

programs.title: Indonesia | Enhanced Due Diligence for High-Risk Customers
programs.why: Banks must have a risk management system to identify high-risk customers and beneficial owners and apply EDD to them. Staff who classify customers and perform EDD need the knowledge to do so; no separate EDD course is prescribed.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Banks need risk criteria for high-risk customers, apply EDD to them, and for PEPs obtain senior approval, check source of funds and wealth and monitor more closely.

programs.title: Indonesia | Ongoing Monitoring and Data Updating
programs.why: Banks must monitor relationships to confirm transactions fit the customer's profile and source of funds, update customer data when changes are found, and report annual data-updating plans and results to OJK.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Banks must monitor customer transactions against their profile, update and document customer data, and submit yearly data-updating plans and realisation reports to OJK.

programs.title: Indonesia | Beneficial Owner Identification and Verification
programs.why: Banks must establish whether a customer acts for itself or for a beneficial owner and apply CDD or EDD to that owner. Corporate onboarding staff need to understand ownership and control structures to meet this duty.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Banks must confirm whether customers act on their own behalf or for a beneficial owner and carry out CDD or EDD on the beneficial owner.

programs.title: Indonesia | Politically Exposed Persons
programs.why: Foreign and domestic PEPs and those with prominent functions in international organisations require a detection system, approval by a designated senior officer, source of wealth and funds analysis and closer monitoring. Staff and approvers must be able to apply these rules.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Defines PEPs and requires senior-officer approval, periodic EDD on source of funds and wealth, and stricter monitoring for PEP relationships.

programs.title: Indonesia | Sanctions Screening (DTTOT and DPPSPM Lists)
programs.why: Indonesia's sanctions duties for banks centre on the domestic terrorist list and the proliferation-financing list, which banks must keep current and screen against. Screening teams need to handle matches, false positives and escalation correctly.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Banks must keep the DTTOT and DPPSPM lists current, screen customers and beneficial owners against them, and manage false positives and negatives.

references.title: Daftar Terduga Teroris dan Organisasi Teroris (DTTOT) (Domestic list of suspected terrorists and terrorist organisations)
references.issuer: Pusat Pelaporan dan Analisis Transaksi Keuangan (PPATK)
references.note: PPATK explains that Indonesia applies targeted financial sanctions under Law 9/2013 by listing persons and entities in the DTTOT and freezing their funds immediately, with court designation, objection and delisting procedures.

programs.title: Indonesia | Targeted Financial Sanctions and Immediate Freezing
programs.why: Under Law 9/2013 the funds of persons and entities on the court-confirmed terrorist list must be frozen at once, and OJK guidance sets out how banks do this and report it. Staff who operate the freeze need to know the steps, timing and reporting lines.

references.title: Undang-Undang Nomor 9 Tahun 2013 tentang Pencegahan dan Pemberantasan Tindak Pidana Pendanaan Terorisme (Law 9/2013 on the Prevention and Eradication of Terrorism Financing)
references.issuer: Republic of Indonesia (copy published by OJK)
references.note: Funds of listed persons and corporations must be frozen immediately on receipt of the court designation, and the freeze lasts while they remain listed; objections go to the national police chief.

references.title: SEOJK Nomor 38/SEOJK.01/2017 tentang Pedoman Pemblokiran Secara Serta Merta atas Dana Nasabah di Sektor Jasa Keuangan yang Identitasnya Tercantum dalam DTTOT (OJK Circular 38/2017: immediate freezing)
references.note: Step-by-step guidance for freezing, without delay, the funds of customers named on the domestic terrorist list (DTTOT) and reporting the freeze; issued under the 2017 POJK and kept alive by POJK 8/2023 where consistent with it.

references.title: Daftar Terduga Teroris dan Organisasi Teroris (DTTOT) (Domestic list of suspected terrorists and terrorist organisations)
references.issuer: Pusat Pelaporan dan Analisis Transaksi Keuangan (PPATK)
references.note: PPATK explains that Indonesia applies targeted financial sanctions under Law 9/2013 by listing persons and entities in the DTTOT and freezing their funds immediately, with court designation, objection and delisting procedures.

programs.title: Indonesia | Suspicious Transaction Reporting to PPATK
programs.why: Law 8/2010 and Law 9/2013 require suspicious transaction reports to PPATK within three working days and protect reporters acting in good faith, while tipping off is a crime. POJK 8/2023 training must cover the AML/CFT laws, typologies and each employee's role, so every employee learns to recognise and escalate suspicion.

references.title: Undang-Undang Nomor 8 Tahun 2010 tentang Pencegahan dan Pemberantasan Tindak Pidana Pencucian Uang (Law 8/2010 on the Prevention and Eradication of Money Laundering)
references.issuer: Republic of Indonesia (copy published by OJK)
references.note: Suspicious transactions must be reported to PPATK as soon as possible and no later than three working days after the bank knows of them; reporting overrides secrecy and reporters are protected from liability.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Banks must train officers and staff on AML, CFT and CPF at least once a year, more often where risk or major changes call for it; content covers the laws, ML/TF/PF typologies, internal policies and each employee's role, and training must be evaluated.

references.title: Pedoman Pelaporan (PPATK reporting guidance for reporting parties)
references.issuer: Pusat Pelaporan dan Analisis Transaksi Keuangan (PPATK)
references.note: Lists the reporting parties and explains the report types financial service providers file with PPATK (suspicious, large cash and cross-border transfer reports) and what makes a transaction suspicious.

programs.title: Indonesia | Transaction Monitoring and Alert Handling
programs.why: Banks must have a management information system able to identify, analyse and monitor transactions and must monitor relationships against customer profiles. The AML officer must analyse unit reports and prepare suspicious transaction reports, so analysts need practical monitoring skills.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: The AML officer analyses and compiles suspicious and cash transaction reports; banks must monitor transactions against profiles and maintain a monitoring information system.

programs.title: Indonesia | Cross-Border Correspondent Banking
audience: Correspondent banking and financial institutions teams
programs.why: Before offering cross-border correspondent services a commercial bank must understand the respondent bank's business, reputation and the AML/CFT/CPF standards of its home country. Staff in this area need to know these due diligence steps.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Before providing cross-border correspondent banking, the bank must gather information on the respondent's profile, reputation and the AML/CFT/CPF regime of its home country.

programs.title: Indonesia | Individual Risk Assessment and Risk-Based Approach
programs.why: Banks must identify, assess and document ML/TF/PF risk across customers, geography, products and channels, refresh the assessment every year and send it to OJK by the end of June. New products and technologies must be risk-assessed before launch. These duties need staff who understand the risk-based approach.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Banks document an individual ML/TF/PF risk assessment, update it once a year, assess new products and technologies before launch, and report the updated assessment to OJK each June.

programs.title: Indonesia | AML Record Keeping and Regulatory Reporting
programs.why: Customer and transaction records must be kept for at least five years after the relationship ends, and documents must be produced to OJK or other authorities within three working days of a request. Banks also file cash and cross-border transfer reports to PPATK within fourteen working days.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Customer records must be kept for at least five years after the relationship ends or after a mismatch is found, and supplied to OJK or other authorities within three working days of a request.

references.title: Undang-Undang Nomor 8 Tahun 2010 tentang Pencegahan dan Pemberantasan Tindak Pidana Pencucian Uang (Law 8/2010 on the Prevention and Eradication of Money Laundering)
references.issuer: Republic of Indonesia (copy published by OJK)
references.note: Identity records must be kept for at least five years after the relationship ends; cash and cross-border transfer reports are due within fourteen working days.

programs.title: Indonesia | AML/CFT Training for Front-Line Staff and New Joiners
programs.why: POJK 8/2023 singles out employees of relevant work units and new employees as those directors must ensure have completed AML/CFT/CPF training, at least once a year. The same chapter requires pre-employment screening and know-your-employee monitoring for staff from the lowest grade up.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Directors must ensure officers and staff, particularly those in relevant units and new joiners, attend AML/CFT/CPF training once a year.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Banks must screen new hires, monitor employee profiles (know your employee) and provide at least annual AML/CFT/CPF training whose effectiveness is evaluated.

programs.title: Indonesia | AML/CFT Oversight for Directors and Commissioners
programs.why: Active oversight by the Board of Directors and the Board of Commissioners is the first pillar of the programme: directors propose and enforce policies, appoint the AML unit or officer and discuss AML matters at board meetings, while commissioners approve and supervise. The AML officer must have adequate capability. These are competence expectations rather than a prescribed course for the boards.

references.title: POJK Nomor 8 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Program Anti Pencucian Uang, Pencegahan Pendanaan Terorisme, dan Pencegahan Pendanaan Proliferasi Senjata Pemusnah Massal di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 8/2023: AML, CFT and CPF programmes)
references.note: Directors propose policies, set up the AML unit or officer, oversee compliance and discuss AML at board meetings; commissioners approve and oversee; the AML officer must be capable and have full data access.

programs.title: Indonesia | Anti-Bribery and Corruption within the OJK Anti-Fraud Strategy
programs.why: POJK 12/2024 classes corruption, including bribery, conflicts of interest, illegal gratuities and extortion, as fraud. Banks must educate and develop the competence of internal staff on their anti-fraud policy at least once a year, so bribery and corruption content belongs in that yearly programme.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 12 Tahun 2024 tentang Penerapan Strategi Anti Fraud bagi Lembaga Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 12/2024 on anti-fraud strategy for financial services institutions)
references.note: Fraud includes corruption such as bribery, conflicts of interest, illicit receipts and extortion; institutions must educate and build the competence of internal parties on the anti-fraud policy at least once a year.

programs.title: Indonesia | Anti-Fraud Strategy: Prevention, Detection and Reporting
programs.why: POJK 12/2024 requires an anti-fraud strategy built on prevention, detection, investigation and monitoring, a dedicated anti-fraud unit or function, fraud reporting to OJK and at least annual education for internal staff on the anti-fraud policy. Its attachment expects anti-fraud awareness programmes and know-your-employee measures.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 12 Tahun 2024 tentang Penerapan Strategi Anti Fraud bagi Lembaga Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 12/2024 on anti-fraud strategy for financial services institutions)
references.note: The strategy has four pillars; institutions must run anti-fraud education and competence development for staff at least yearly and have a unit or function responsible for the strategy.

programs.title: Indonesia | Good Corporate Governance for Commercial Banks (POJK 17/2023)
programs.why: POJK 17/2023 is the umbrella governance rule for commercial banks, covering board structure, committees, compliance, audit, risk management, remuneration and conflicts of interest. It requires integrity and competence of board members but does not prescribe a separate governance course.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 17 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Tata Kelola bagi Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 17/2023 on governance of commercial banks)
references.note: Directors must keep integrity, competence and good reputation while in office; independent commissioners need adequate banking knowledge and experience.

programs.title: Indonesia | Risk Management Certification for Directors and Commissioners
audience: Independent members of the risk monitoring committee
programs.why: Under POJK 24/2022 and SEOJK 28/2022, board members must hold a valid banking risk management certificate for as long as they serve. Certificates last three years and are extended through at least yearly refresher programmes; banks must replace members who let them lapse. Certificate holding also feeds into OJK's fit and proper assessment.

references.title: Surat Edaran OJK Nomor 28/SEOJK.03/2022 tentang Sertifikasi Manajemen Risiko bagi Sumber Daya Manusia Bank Umum (OJK Circular 28/2022 on risk management certification for commercial bank staff)
references.note: Directors, commissioners and executive officers must hold a valid risk management certificate while in post; certificates last three years and can be extended through refresher programmes held at least yearly.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 24 Tahun 2022 tentang Pengembangan Kualitas Sumber Daya Manusia Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 24/2022 on developing the quality of commercial bank human resources)
references.note: Banks must run the banking competency certification set by OJK, including risk management, and monitor that staff hold certificates and follow periodic maintenance programmes.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 17 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Tata Kelola bagi Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 17/2023 on governance of commercial banks)
references.note: Independent members of the risk monitoring committee must hold a risk management certificate equal to that required of directors.

programs.title: Indonesia | Executive Officers: Critical Roles and Certification
programs.why: Banks must identify critical functions and positions, and the people in them must have the required competence. Executive officers must also hold a valid risk management certificate while in post, maintained through yearly refreshers.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 24 Tahun 2022 tentang Pengembangan Kualitas Sumber Daya Manusia Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 24/2022 on developing the quality of commercial bank human resources)
references.note: Banks must identify critical functions and positions, and directors and officers in critical positions must have the competence those roles require; OJK can evaluate this.

references.title: Surat Edaran OJK Nomor 28/SEOJK.03/2022 tentang Sertifikasi Manajemen Risiko bagi Sumber Daya Manusia Bank Umum (OJK Circular 28/2022 on risk management certification for commercial bank staff)
references.note: Executive officers must hold a risk management certificate that remains valid while in post.

programs.title: Indonesia | Fit and Proper Requirements for Bank Leaders
programs.why: Directors and commissioners must pass OJK's fit and proper assessment and keep integrity, competence and a good reputation while in office. Holding a risk management certificate is one of the competence factors OJK considers.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 17 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Tata Kelola bagi Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 17/2023 on governance of commercial banks)
references.note: Directors must meet OJK approval requirements and maintain integrity, competence and good reputation while in office.

references.title: Surat Edaran OJK Nomor 28/SEOJK.03/2022 tentang Sertifikasi Manajemen Risiko bagi Sumber Daya Manusia Bank Umum (OJK Circular 28/2022 on risk management certification for commercial bank staff)
references.note: A risk management certificate is part of the competence assessment for candidate directors and commissioners.

programs.title: Indonesia | Whistleblowing under the Anti-Fraud Strategy
programs.why: The detection pillar of POJK 12/2024 expects a clear whistleblowing policy with reporter protection that encourages employees and outsiders to report fraud. Staff must know how to report and how reporters are protected; the regulation's annual anti-fraud education can carry this content.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 12 Tahun 2024 tentang Penerapan Strategi Anti Fraud bagi Lembaga Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 12/2024 on anti-fraud strategy for financial services institutions)
references.note: The detection pillar includes a whistleblowing policy and mechanism, including protection of whistleblowers, designed to encourage staff and outsiders to report fraud.

programs.title: Indonesia | Consumer and Public Protection (POJK 22/2023)
programs.why: POJK 22/2023 requires banks to build staff capacity on consumer protection through training: at least yearly for the consumer protection unit and at least once during employment for everyone else. Content covers complaint procedures, the unit's duties, product knowledge and ethical communication with consumers, and training must be evaluated.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 22 Tahun 2023 tentang Pelindungan Konsumen dan Masyarakat di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 22/2023 on consumer and public protection in the financial services sector)
references.note: Banks must train staff on consumer protection: yearly for the consumer protection unit, at least once in their service for other staff, with set content and evaluation of results.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 22 Tahun 2023 tentang Pelindungan Konsumen dan Masyarakat di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 22/2023 on consumer and public protection in the financial services sector)
references.note: Banks must apply the consumer protection principles in all business activities.

references.title: Undang-Undang Nomor 4 Tahun 2023 tentang Pengembangan dan Penguatan Sektor Keuangan (Law 4/2023 on Financial Sector Development and Strengthening, P2SK)
references.issuer: Republic of Indonesia (copy published by Bank Indonesia)
references.note: Financial sector actors are responsible for developing staff competence through continuous education and training and must budget for it each year.

programs.title: Indonesia | Clear Product Information and Disclosure
programs.why: Banks must give clear, accurate, honest and accessible product information before and during the relationship, state in all offers that they are licensed and supervised by OJK, and design products for a defined target market. Staff explaining products need enough product knowledge to do so.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 22 Tahun 2023 tentang Pelindungan Konsumen dan Masyarakat di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 22/2023 on consumer and public protection in the financial services sector)
references.note: Products must be designed for target consumers; information must be clear, accurate, honest and accessible; marketing must name the bank and state that it is OJK licensed and supervised.

programs.title: Indonesia | Complaint Handling and Resolution
programs.why: Each bank office must have a function that receives and resolves complaints, staffed by people with product and complaint-handling knowledge and authority. Complaints must be resolved within set deadlines. The consumer protection unit must be trained yearly, and front-line complaint staff before placement.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 22 Tahun 2023 tentang Pelindungan Konsumen dan Masyarakat di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 22/2023 on consumer and public protection in the financial services sector)
references.note: Complaint staff must have product and complaint-handling knowledge and authority; consumer protection unit staff are trained yearly, and the elucidation expects training before placement.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 22 Tahun 2023 tentang Pelindungan Konsumen dan Masyarakat di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 22/2023 on consumer and public protection in the financial services sector)
references.note: Complaints must be followed up and resolved within the deadline set by the regulation.

references.title: Peraturan Bank Indonesia Nomor 3 Tahun 2023 tentang Pelindungan Konsumen Bank Indonesia (Bank Indonesia Regulation 3/2023 on Bank Indonesia consumer protection)
references.note: For activities Bank Indonesia supervises (such as payment services), providers need competent staff, and staff in education, consumer-data protection and complaint-handling functions must attend supporting training.

programs.title: Indonesia | Suitability and Mis-selling Prevention
programs.why: Banks must match products to each prospect's needs and ability, based on a documented consumer classification, and may not exploit customers who have no real choice or sell unlicensed products. Sales staff need to understand and document suitability assessments.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 22 Tahun 2023 tentang Pelindungan Konsumen dan Masyarakat di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 22/2023 on consumer and public protection in the financial services sector)
references.note: Banks may not exploit consumers' circumstances or sell unlicensed products, and must assess and document whether a product suits the prospect's needs and capacity.

programs.title: Indonesia | Fair Access for Consumers with Disabilities and Older Consumers
programs.why: Banks must provide information services and equal access to consumers and are responsible for supporting special services for people with disabilities and older consumers. Front-line staff need the awareness to serve these customers appropriately.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 22 Tahun 2023 tentang Pelindungan Konsumen dan Masyarakat di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 22/2023 on consumer and public protection in the financial services sector)
references.note: Banks must provide information services and equal access, and support special services for consumers with disabilities and older consumers.

programs.title: Indonesia | Customer Data Confidentiality and Bank Secrecy
programs.why: Banks must keep consumer data and information confidential and use it only with consent or as the law allows. The Banking Law, as amended by the P2SK Law, keeps depositor information secret subject to listed exceptions. Staff handling data need to know these limits.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 22 Tahun 2023 tentang Pelindungan Konsumen dan Masyarakat di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 22/2023 on consumer and public protection in the financial services sector)
references.note: Banks must protect the confidentiality of consumers' personal data and information and may share data only within data protection rules and OJK requirements.

references.title: Undang-Undang Nomor 4 Tahun 2023 tentang Pengembangan dan Penguatan Sektor Keuangan (Law 4/2023 on Financial Sector Development and Strengthening, P2SK)
references.issuer: Republic of Indonesia (copy published by Bank Indonesia)
references.provision: Article 14 (amending Articles 40 to 40C of the Banking Law)
references.note: Banks and affiliated parties must keep depositor information confidential, with exceptions such as court cases, tax information requests and written customer consent.

references.title: Undang-Undang Nomor 27 Tahun 2022 tentang Pelindungan Data Pribadi (Law 27/2022 on Personal Data Protection)
references.issuer: Republic of Indonesia (JDIH BPK legislation portal)
references.note: The general personal data protection law that applies to banks as data controllers; the official text could not be opened in this review (portal blocks automated access), so no provision is cited.

programs.title: Indonesia | Debt Collection Conduct and Certified Collectors
programs.why: Banks must send warning letters with set content before collecting overdue credit. Where they use third-party collectors, the agency must be a licensed legal entity whose staff hold debt collection certification from a professional certification body registered with OJK, and collection must follow conduct rules on methods and hours.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 22 Tahun 2023 tentang Pelindungan Konsumen dan Masyarakat di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 22/2023 on consumer and public protection in the financial services sector)
references.note: Overdue borrowers must receive warning letters; outsourced collectors must be licensed entities with staff certified in collection, and collection must avoid threats or violence and respect set hours.

programs.title: Indonesia | Responsible Sales and Marketing Practices
programs.why: Offers through private channels need the consumer's consent, may be made only on set days and hours, and must identify the bank, explain the purpose and disclose the source of the consumer's data. Suitability must be assessed and documented before sale.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 22 Tahun 2023 tentang Pelindungan Konsumen dan Masyarakat di Sektor Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 22/2023 on consumer and public protection in the financial services sector)
references.note: Banks need consent before offering through personal communication channels, must respect contact hours and stop when consent is withdrawn, and must assess suitability.

programs.title: Indonesia | Information Security Awareness (PADK 1/2026)
programs.why: PADK 1/2026, which implements POJK 11/2022, expects the information security policy to include a security awareness programme and requires training or briefings on information security for bank employees, consultants, temporary staff and IT service provider staff, tailored to their roles. Directors must ensure staff competence through training and awareness education.

references.title: Peraturan Anggota Dewan Komisioner OJK Nomor 1 Tahun 2026 tentang Penyelenggaraan Teknologi Informasi oleh Bank Umum (OJK Board Member Regulation 1/2026 on IT operation by commercial banks)
references.provision: Attachment, Information Security: security policy and HR management procedure
references.note: The security policy covers training and awareness; security training or briefings must be given to employees, consultants, temporary staff and provider staff according to their roles.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 11/POJK.03/2022 tentang Penyelenggaraan Teknologi Informasi oleh Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 11/2022 on the use of information technology by commercial banks)
references.note: Banks must map and set IT governance aspects including supporting human resources and IT culture.

programs.title: Indonesia | Cyber Security Awareness for Bank Staff
programs.why: SEOJK 29/2022 implements the cyber resilience duty in POJK 11/2022. Its assessment criteria expect directors to build cyber security awareness across all staff, through an awareness programme run regularly and at least annually, and to run continuing capacity programmes covering phishing, social engineering, data leakage and incident response for relevant staff including the boards. The yearly awareness programme and phishing simulation appear in SEOJK 29/2022's maturity-assessment criteria (Attachment I.b) rather than as binding rules, so this is classified as a competence expectation.

references.title: Surat Edaran OJK Nomor 29/SEOJK.03/2022 tentang Ketahanan dan Keamanan Siber bagi Bank Umum (OJK Circular 29/2022 on cyber resilience and security for commercial banks)
references.note: Directors should build awareness through a programme run at least once a year and verify it, for example with annual phishing simulations; banks should run continuing cyber capacity programmes for relevant staff including the boards.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 11/POJK.03/2022 tentang Penyelenggaraan Teknologi Informasi oleh Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 11/2022 on the use of information technology by commercial banks)
references.note: Banks must maintain cyber resilience by identifying, protecting, detecting and responding to cyber incidents.

programs.title: Indonesia | Cyber Security Risk Management
programs.why: Banks must maintain cyber resilience, test cyber security, assess cyber maturity and set up an independent unit or function for cyber resilience and security. Staff in these functions must be competent; SEOJK 29/2022 expects recruitment, development and training systems that ensure competent cyber risk staff.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 11/POJK.03/2022 tentang Penyelenggaraan Teknologi Informasi oleh Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 11/2022 on the use of information technology by commercial banks)
references.note: Banks must keep cyber resilience, assess maturity, test security and maintain an independent cyber security unit or function.

references.title: Surat Edaran OJK Nomor 29/SEOJK.03/2022 tentang Ketahanan dan Keamanan Siber bagi Bank Umum (OJK Circular 29/2022 on cyber resilience and security for commercial banks)
references.note: Directors should set up recruitment, development and training systems so that competent cyber risk staff are available.

programs.title: Indonesia | Personal Data Protection in Bank IT
programs.why: POJK 11/2022 requires banks to manage data effectively and apply personal data protection principles in processing, including impact assessments for high-risk processing and controls on data sharing. Law 27/2022 sets the general data protection regime.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 11/POJK.03/2022 tentang Penyelenggaraan Teknologi Informasi oleh Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 11/2022 on the use of information technology by commercial banks)
references.note: Banks must manage data effectively, apply personal data protection principles, assess impact where processing raises risk, and set controls for data exchange.

references.title: Peraturan Anggota Dewan Komisioner OJK Nomor 1 Tahun 2026 tentang Penyelenggaraan Teknologi Informasi oleh Bank Umum (OJK Board Member Regulation 1/2026 on IT operation by commercial banks)
references.provision: Attachment, data management and personal data protection
references.note: Gives further detail on data management and personal data protection in bank IT operations.

references.title: Undang-Undang Nomor 27 Tahun 2022 tentang Pelindungan Data Pribadi (Law 27/2022 on Personal Data Protection)
references.issuer: Republic of Indonesia (JDIH BPK legislation portal)
references.note: The general personal data protection law that applies to banks as data controllers; the official text could not be opened in this review (portal blocks automated access), so no provision is cited.

programs.title: Indonesia | IT and Cyber Incident Reporting to OJK
audience: IT operations and incident response teams
programs.why: Significant IT incidents must be notified to OJK within 24 hours of discovery and reported in full within five working days, and SEOJK 29/2022 applies the same sequence to cyber incidents. Incident teams must know the triggers and formats.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 11/POJK.03/2022 tentang Penyelenggaraan Teknologi Informasi oleh Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 11/2022 on the use of information technology by commercial banks)
references.note: For IT incidents that may cause significant loss or disruption, banks give an initial notice within 24 hours and a full report within five working days.

references.title: Surat Edaran OJK Nomor 29/SEOJK.03/2022 tentang Ketahanan dan Keamanan Siber bagi Bank Umum (OJK Circular 29/2022 on cyber resilience and security for commercial banks)
references.note: Initial notice of a cyber incident goes to the bank's OJK supervisor within 24 hours of discovery, followed by a cyber incident report.

programs.title: Indonesia | Data Breach Management
programs.why: A personal data breach in a bank is handled as an IT or cyber incident with OJK notification deadlines, and must also be managed under the personal data protection law, whose text could not be opened here. Response teams need to coordinate both tracks.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 11/POJK.03/2022 tentang Penyelenggaraan Teknologi Informasi oleh Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 11/2022 on the use of information technology by commercial banks)
references.note: Initial notice to OJK within 24 hours and a full report within five working days for significant IT incidents.

references.title: Undang-Undang Nomor 27 Tahun 2022 tentang Pelindungan Data Pribadi (Law 27/2022 on Personal Data Protection)
references.issuer: Republic of Indonesia (JDIH BPK legislation portal)
references.note: The general personal data protection law that applies to banks as data controllers; the official text could not be opened in this review (portal blocks automated access), so no provision is cited.

programs.title: Indonesia | Cyber Resilience and Operational Continuity
programs.why: POJK 11/2022 frames cyber resilience as identifying assets and threats, protecting assets, detecting incidents and responding and recovering, supported by an information system for cyber resilience. Staff running these processes need the related skills.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 11/POJK.03/2022 tentang Penyelenggaraan Teknologi Informasi oleh Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 11/2022 on the use of information technology by commercial banks)
references.note: Banks must maintain cyber resilience through identification, protection, detection, response and recovery, supported by an adequate information system.

programs.title: Indonesia | IT Governance and IT Risk Management
programs.why: POJK 11/2022 and PADK 1/2026 set the duties of directors, commissioners, the IT steering committee and IT units and require an IT risk management process. Directors are expected to ensure IT risk awareness across all levels, which may be done through a risk awareness programme.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 11/POJK.03/2022 tentang Penyelenggaraan Teknologi Informasi oleh Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 11/2022 on the use of information technology by commercial banks)
references.note: Banks must set IT governance aspects including human resources and IT culture; directors carry defined IT responsibilities.

references.title: Peraturan Anggota Dewan Komisioner OJK Nomor 1 Tahun 2026 tentang Penyelenggaraan Teknologi Informasi oleh Bank Umum (OJK Board Member Regulation 1/2026 on IT operation by commercial banks)
references.provision: Attachment, IT risk management: risk identification
references.note: Directors should ensure IT risk awareness at all levels, for example through a risk awareness programme for staff and management.

programs.title: Indonesia | Risk Management Certification for Officers in Risk-Taking Units
audience: Risk management, compliance and internal audit officers
Credit, treasury, IT and finance officers
programs.why: SEOJK 28/2022 requires officers below executive level in the risk management, compliance and internal audit units, and in key operating units such as credit, treasury, IT and finance, to hold a valid risk management certificate. Certificates last three years and may be extended by refreshers taken at least once a year.

references.title: Surat Edaran OJK Nomor 28/SEOJK.03/2022 tentang Sertifikasi Manajemen Risiko bagi Sumber Daya Manusia Bank Umum (OJK Circular 28/2022 on risk management certification for commercial bank staff)
references.note: Officers in risk, compliance, audit and main risk-taking units must hold a risk management certificate; validity is three years, extendable through refreshers held at least once a year.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 24 Tahun 2022 tentang Pengembangan Kualitas Sumber Daya Manusia Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 24/2022 on developing the quality of commercial bank human resources)
references.note: Banks must budget at least 3.5 percent of the prior year's gross salary cost for staff development each year and carry out OJK-set banking competency certification.

programs.title: Indonesia | Risk Management Training for Business, Risk and Audit Units (POJK 18/2016)
programs.why: OJK's risk management rule makes directors responsible for raising the risk management competence of staff, and the standard guideline attached to OJK Circular 34/2016 spells out that the competence of leaders and personnel in business units, the risk management unit and internal audit must be built through continuous education and training. Operational risk sits at the centre of this: business units own their operational risks day to day and the risk unit supports them with operational risk training.

references.title: Lampiran I Surat Edaran OJK Nomor 34/SEOJK.03/2016 tentang Penerapan Manajemen Risiko bagi Bank Umum (Annex I to OJK Circular 34/2016: standard risk management guideline for commercial banks)
references.provision: Part I.A.2 (human resources), points c and d; Part II.D (operational risk), organisation point
references.note: Directors must set up recruitment, development and training systems and must raise the competence of business, risk and audit unit staff through continuous education and training; the operational risk function supports business units with training.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 18/POJK.03/2016 tentang Penerapan Manajemen Risiko bagi Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 18/2016 on risk management for commercial banks)
references.note: Directors must ensure the competence of risk management staff improves, the elucidation pointing to continuous education and training programmes.

programs.title: Indonesia | Credit Risk Management under POJK 18/2016
programs.why: Credit risk is one of the eight risks every commercial bank must manage under POJK 18/2016, with board oversight, written policies and limits, measurement, monitoring and internal control. The standard guideline expects staff in each unit to understand the risks of the products they handle. No separate credit risk course is prescribed beyond the general risk management training duty.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 18/POJK.03/2016 tentang Penerapan Manajemen Risiko bagi Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 18/2016 on risk management for commercial banks)
references.note: Banks must apply effective risk management to credit, market, liquidity, operational, legal, reputation, strategic and compliance risk, covering oversight, policies and limits, risk processes and internal control.

references.title: Lampiran I Surat Edaran OJK Nomor 34/SEOJK.03/2016 tentang Penerapan Manajemen Risiko bagi Bank Umum (Annex I to OJK Circular 34/2016: standard risk management guideline for commercial banks)
references.provision: Part I.A.2 point f; Part II.A (credit risk)
references.note: Staff placed in each unit must understand the risks inherent in the bank's products and activities; Part II.A sets the credit risk management standard.

programs.title: Indonesia | Market Risk Management and Treasury Controls
programs.why: Banks with trading or banking book exposures to interest rate, exchange rate, equity or commodity movements must measure and limit market risk, including interest rate risk in the banking book, and run stress tests and shock simulations. Staff in treasury and market risk need to understand the measurement methods, limits and escalation lines that OJK's standard guideline sets.

references.title: Lampiran I Surat Edaran OJK Nomor 34/SEOJK.03/2016 tentang Penerapan Manajemen Risiko bagi Bank Umum (Annex I to OJK Circular 34/2016: standard risk management guideline for commercial banks)
references.provision: Part II.B (market risk), risk identification and measurement
references.note: Banks must identify market risk sources, including repricing, yield curve, basis and optionality risk in the banking book, and must stress test and shock-simulate interest rate risk in the banking book.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 18/POJK.03/2016 tentang Penerapan Manajemen Risiko bagi Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 18/2016 on risk management for commercial banks)
references.note: Market risk is one of the risks the bank must manage.

programs.title: Indonesia | Liquidity Risk, LCR and ILAAP (POJK 42/2015 as amended by POJK 19/2024)
programs.why: Conventional commercial banks must meet the liquidity coverage ratio, monitor liquidity indicators and, since the 2024 amendment, run an internal liquidity adequacy assessment process (ILAAP) proportionate to their size. OJK Circular 26/2025 sets the ILAAP method, including intraday liquidity and liquidity stress testing, with reporting phased in from December 2026. The standard guideline requires units managing liquidity risk, such as ALCO, treasury and the dealing room, to be staffed with competent people.

references.title: POJK Nomor 19 Tahun 2024 tentang Perubahan atas POJK Nomor 42/POJK.03/2015 tentang Kewajiban Pemenuhan Rasio Kecukupan Likuiditas bagi Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 19/2024 amending the LCR rule)
references.note: Besides calculating the LCR, banks must monitor liquidity with set indicators and carry out an ILAAP suited to their size and complexity, by a method OJK sets.

references.title: Surat Edaran OJK Nomor 26/SEOJK.03/2025 tentang Proses Asesmen Kecukupan Likuiditas secara Internal (Internal Liquidity Adequacy Assessment Process) bagi Bank Umum (OJK Circular 26/2025 on ILAAP)
references.note: Sets how banks carry out and report their ILAAP, including the liquidity stress testing framework, intraday liquidity and the use of stress results.

references.title: Lampiran I Surat Edaran OJK Nomor 34/SEOJK.03/2016 tentang Penerapan Manajemen Risiko bagi Bank Umum (Annex I to OJK Circular 34/2016: standard risk management guideline for commercial banks)
references.provision: Part II.C (liquidity risk), human resources point
references.note: Directors must ensure every function managing liquidity risk, such as ALCO, treasury and the dealing room, has staff of adequate competence.

programs.title: Indonesia | Stress Testing in Risk and Liquidity Management
programs.why: OJK's standard guideline expects banks to stress test regularly, review the results and act when projected losses exceed their tolerance, feeding results into policies and limits. The ILAAP circular adds a liquidity stress testing framework and requires banks to explain how stress results are used. Staff who design scenarios and act on results need to understand these expectations; no separate course is prescribed.

references.title: Lampiran I Surat Edaran OJK Nomor 34/SEOJK.03/2016 tentang Penerapan Manajemen Risiko bagi Bank Umum (Annex I to OJK Circular 34/2016: standard risk management guideline for commercial banks)
references.provision: Part I.C, points g and h
references.note: Stress testing complements risk measurement; banks should stress test periodically, review results and use them when setting or changing policies and limits.

references.title: Surat Edaran OJK Nomor 26/SEOJK.03/2025 tentang Proses Asesmen Kecukupan Likuiditas secara Internal (Internal Liquidity Adequacy Assessment Process) bagi Bank Umum (OJK Circular 26/2025 on ILAAP)
references.note: The ILAAP covers a liquidity stress testing framework, stress results and their main risk drivers, and intraday liquidity stress testing.

programs.title: Indonesia | Legal Lending Limit (BMPK) and Large Exposures
programs.why: Commercial banks must calculate the legal lending limit (Batas Maksimum Pemberian Kredit, BMPK) and large exposures for every provision of funds, individually and on a consolidated basis, and must have written policies, guidelines and procedures for lending to related parties and large exposures. Staff structuring or approving facilities must know the limits and related-party rules; no training duty is stated.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 32/POJK.03/2018 tentang Batas Maksimum Pemberian Kredit dan Penyediaan Dana Besar bagi Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 32/2018 on legal lending limits and large exposures)
references.note: Banks must calculate BMPK and large exposures individually and consolidated, apply prudence to related-party and large exposures, and keep written policies, guidelines and procedures for them.

programs.title: Indonesia | Country and Transfer Risk Management (PADK 10/2026)
programs.why: A 2026 OJK rule makes country and transfer risk part of credit risk management. Banks calculate a country and transfer risk ratio each half year, fall into one of three groups, and must apply general or stricter risk management and qualitative and quantitative reporting depending on the group. The first calculation is for June 2027 data. Staff handling cross-border exposures need to understand the ratio, grouping and reporting.

references.title: Peraturan Anggota Dewan Komisioner OJK Nomor 10 Tahun 2026 tentang Penerapan Manajemen Risiko Country Risk dan Transfer Risk bagi Bank Umum (OJK Board Member Regulation 10/2026 on country and transfer risk management)
references.note: Country and transfer risk is managed within credit risk; banks are grouped by a semi-annual ratio that sets the depth of risk management and reporting, starting with June 2027 data, and the matching parts of SEOJK 34/2016 are replaced.

programs.title: Indonesia | IT Service Provider and Outsourcing Oversight
programs.why: Banks using IT service providers must follow defined steps for identifying needs, selecting providers and managing their risk, and must be able to supervise outsourced activities. POJK 24/2022 also requires banks to ensure outsourced staff are competent for the work.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 11/POJK.03/2022 tentang Penyelenggaraan Teknologi Informasi oleh Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 11/2022 on the use of information technology by commercial banks)
references.note: Banks must identify needs, select providers on set criteria including staff competence, manage provider risk and assess provider performance.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 24 Tahun 2022 tentang Pengembangan Kualitas Sumber Daya Manusia Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 24/2022 on developing the quality of commercial bank human resources)
references.note: Banks must ensure outsourced personnel have the competence the outsourced work requires.

programs.title: Indonesia | Disaster Recovery and Business Continuity
programs.why: Banks must have a disaster recovery plan that works in practice, so operations continue during disasters or IT disruption, and must test it on all critical applications and infrastructure. Staff with recovery roles must know the plan.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 11/POJK.03/2022 tentang Penyelenggaraan Teknologi Informasi oleh Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 11/2022 on the use of information technology by commercial banks)
references.note: Banks must have and be able to execute a disaster recovery plan and test it for all critical applications and infrastructure.

programs.title: Indonesia | Recovery Plans for All Commercial Banks (POJK 5/2024)
programs.why: Since 2024 every commercial bank, not only systemic banks, must prepare a recovery plan, have it approved by shareholders and submit it to OJK, with recovery options tested against capital, liquidity, profitability and asset quality triggers. Banks operating before 31 December 2023 had to submit their first plan by the end of November 2024. Directors and the teams that maintain the plan must understand its triggers and options.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 5 Tahun 2024 tentang Penetapan Status Pengawasan dan Penanganan Permasalahan Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 5/2024 on supervisory status and resolution of problems at commercial banks)
references.note: Every bank must prepare a recovery plan, obtain shareholder approval and submit it to OJK; existing banks had to submit their first plan by the end of November 2024.

programs.title: Indonesia | Bank Credit Policy and Credit Officer Integrity (POJK 42/2017)
programs.why: Every commercial bank must have a written credit policy covering at least the matters in OJK's credit policy guideline. The policy must state that all officials involved in lending, including directors and commissioners, act professionally, honestly and carefully, and fully understand the criminal provision of the Banking Law on improper lending. Credit committee members decide on facilities based on their competence. The rule sets competence and integrity expectations rather than a training course.

references.title: Lampiran Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 42/POJK.03/2017 tentang Kewajiban Penyusunan dan Pelaksanaan Kebijakan Perkreditan atau Pembiayaan Bank bagi Bank Umum (Annex to OJK Regulation 42/2017: guideline for bank credit policies)
references.note: The credit policy must require all lending officials to act professionally and understand the Banking Law's criminal provision on lending; credit committee members decide on the basis of their competence.

programs.title: Indonesia | Asset Quality Classification (POJK 40/2019)
programs.why: OJK's asset quality rule sets how commercial banks classify loans and other earning assets, treat foreclosed collateral, apply accounting standards and use independent appraisers for larger foreclosed assets. Staff who rate debtors and prepare provisioning inputs must apply the criteria consistently; the rule does not prescribe training.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 40/POJK.03/2019 tentang Penilaian Kualitas Aset Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 40/2019 on asset quality assessment for commercial banks)
references.provision: Article 36 and the asset quality chapters
references.note: Sets the asset quality criteria and requires foreclosed assets to be revalued under accounting standards, by an independent appraiser above IDR 5 billion.

programs.title: Indonesia | Loan Restructuring Policy and Decision Rights
programs.why: Banks must have a written restructuring policy approved by commissioners and procedures approved by directors, both under active oversight. Restructuring decisions must be taken by a higher authority than the one that approved the loan, and carried out by staff not involved in the original lending, after analysing the debtor's prospects and repayment capacity. Teams handling restructured loans need to know these separation rules and the accounting treatment.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 40/POJK.03/2019 tentang Penilaian Kualitas Aset Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 40/2019 on asset quality assessment for commercial banks)
references.note: Restructuring follows accounting standards, written policy and procedures with board oversight, decision by a higher authority, execution by uninvolved staff, and cash-flow based analysis.

programs.title: Indonesia | Credit Information Reporting through SLIK
audience: Credit administration and SLIK reporting staff
programs.why: Banks report debtor, facility, collateral, guarantor, owner and financial data to OJK's financial information service (Sistem Layanan Informasi Keuangan, SLIK) every month, completely, accurately and on time. Requests for debtor information must be logged with the requesting employee and may be used only for permitted purposes, and a refusal based on SLIK data must be explained to the applicant in writing. Staff who report or query SLIK need to know these rules.

references.title: POJK Nomor 11 Tahun 2024 tentang Perubahan Kedua atas POJK Nomor 18/POJK.03/2017 tentang Pelaporan dan Permintaan Informasi Debitur melalui SLIK (OJK Regulation 11/2024, second amendment to the SLIK rule)
references.note: Monthly complete and accurate debtor reports; logged requests naming the employee; limits on use of debtor information; written explanation when credit is refused on SLIK data.

programs.title: Indonesia | Payment System Competency Certification (PBI 5/2024)
programs.why: Bank Indonesia requires banks and other payment service providers to ensure that directors, executive officers, supervisors and staff carrying out payment system activities hold a competency-based training certificate or a payment system competency certificate matched to their qualification level, within six months of taking up the role. Certificate holders must refresh their competence at least once every three years, and banks must budget for staff competence. Staff already in post before the rule had until 31 December 2026 to comply.

references.title: Peraturan Bank Indonesia Nomor 5 Tahun 2024 tentang Standardisasi Kompetensi di Bidang Sistem Pembayaran (BI Regulation 5/2024 on competency standards in the payment system field)
references.note: Payment providers must ensure staff doing payment system work hold the required certificate within six months of appointment, refresh it at least every three years and fund staff competence; existing staff had until 31 December 2026.

references.title: Peraturan Anggota Dewan Gubernur Nomor 32 Tahun 2025 tentang Pengaturan Industri Sistem Pembayaran (BI Board Member Regulation 32/2025 on payment system industry rules)
references.note: Payment service providers offering the broader activity bundles must meet payment system staff competence requirements as part of risk management.

programs.title: Indonesia | Digital Financial Services (LKD) Agent Training
programs.why: Payment service providers that issue electronic money through agents under Bank Indonesia's digital financial services scheme (Layanan Keuangan Digital, LKD) must train and educate prospective agents who pass due diligence before issuing an appointment certificate and signing the agreement, and must keep written policies on service scope and agent supervision.

references.title: Peraturan Anggota Dewan Gubernur Nomor 32 Tahun 2025 tentang Pengaturan Industri Sistem Pembayaran (BI Board Member Regulation 32/2025 on payment system industry rules)
references.note: Providers running LKD must give training and education to prospective agents who passed due diligence, and only appoint agents who have completed it.

programs.title: Indonesia | Digital Banking Services (POJK 21/2023)
programs.why: POJK 21/2023 governs digital services offered by commercial banks alone or with partners, including licensing, partnerships, use of IT, electronic signatures, customer protection and personal data. Banks must educate customers on using adequate authentication factors. Staff building and running digital channels need to know these requirements; no staff training duty is set.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 21 Tahun 2023 tentang Layanan Digital oleh Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 21/2023 on digital services by commercial banks)
references.note: Banks must identify and verify digital customers and must educate customers to use adequate authentication factors.

programs.title: Indonesia | Laku Pandai Branchless Banking Agents
programs.why: Banks offering branchless banking (Layanan Keuangan Tanpa Kantor dalam rangka Keuangan Inklusif, Laku Pandai) through agents must vet agents, supervise them and give them education and training regularly and effectively, covering product benefits, costs and risks, operating procedures including the electronic devices used, and customer due diligence. OJK's implementing circular, still in force, requires training before agents start serving customers.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 1/POJK.03/2022 tentang Layanan Keuangan Tanpa Kantor dalam rangka Keuangan Inklusif (OJK Regulation 1/2022 on branchless financial services for financial inclusion, Laku Pandai)
references.note: Banks must educate and train Laku Pandai agents periodically and optimally on products, operating procedures and customer due diligence; the older implementing rules remain in force where consistent.

references.title: Surat Edaran OJK Nomor 6/SEOJK.03/2015 tentang Layanan Keuangan Tanpa Kantor dalam rangka Keuangan Inklusif oleh Bank (OJK Circular 6/2015 on Laku Pandai)
references.provision: Section on training and education for Laku Pandai agents (point C)
references.note: The bank must train agents who pass due diligence, covering service procedures, device use, data security and confidentiality, and complaint handling.

programs.title: Indonesia | Foreign Exchange Transactions against Rupiah (PBI 6/2024)
programs.why: Bank Indonesia's money market and FX market regulation sets the types of FX transactions, the underlying transaction rules and the prohibitions and limits that apply. Banks dealing FX against rupiah must at least confirm that the customer holds a valid underlying transaction where one is required and keep records of it. Front-line and treasury staff need to apply these checks; no training duty is stated.

references.title: Peraturan Bank Indonesia Nomor 6 Tahun 2024 tentang Pasar Uang dan Pasar Valuta Asing (BI Regulation 6/2024 on the money market and foreign exchange market)
references.note: Bank Indonesia sets FX transaction types, underlying requirements and limits; banks dealing FX against rupiah must check and keep records of the underlying transaction.

programs.title: Indonesia | Payment Fraud Management for Payment Service Providers
programs.why: Bank Indonesia's 2025 payment industry rules require payment service providers to run a fraud management system able to detect fraud at account, network and transaction level, to monitor transactions and infrastructure, and to meet payment system staff competence requirements. These framework duties imply that fraud and operations staff understand detection and escalation; no separate fraud course is prescribed by BI.

references.title: Peraturan Anggota Dewan Gubernur Nomor 32 Tahun 2025 tentang Pengaturan Industri Sistem Pembayaran (BI Board Member Regulation 32/2025 on payment system industry rules)
references.note: Providers must have a fraud management system detecting fraud at account, network and transaction level and must meet payment system staff competence requirements.

programs.title: Indonesia | Prudential Reporting through APOLO (POJK 22/2025)
programs.why: Banks must prepare and submit reports to OJK online through OJK's reporting system (APOLO) completely, accurately, currently and on time, correct errors through the same system, and appoint a permanent employee as reporting officer who verifies submissions and manages user access. POJK 22/2025 replaced POJK 63/2020 in October 2025. The rule sets responsibilities rather than training.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 22 Tahun 2025 tentang Pelaporan Bank Umum melalui Sistem Pelaporan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK Regulation 22/2025 on commercial bank reporting through the OJK reporting system)
references.note: Reports must be complete, accurate, current and timely through the OJK system; a permanent employee is appointed as reporting officer; POJK 63/2020 is revoked.

programs.title: Indonesia | FATCA Reporting through OJK
programs.why: Under POJK 25/2019, banks report financial account information on customers who are tax residents of partner jurisdictions, including under the intergovernmental FATCA arrangement with the United States, to the Indonesian tax authority via OJK's online system, with nil reports where nothing is reportable. Staff must apply due diligence and reporting procedures correctly.

references.title: POJK Nomor 25/POJK.03/2019 tentang Pelaporan Informasi Nasabah Asing Terkait Perpajakan kepada Negara Mitra atau Yurisdiksi Mitra (OJK Regulation 25/2019: foreign customer tax reporting)
references.note: Reporting banks must file information on reportable financial accounts, including holder identity, balance and income, or a nil report, through the online system.

programs.title: Indonesia | Common Reporting Standard (AEOI) Reporting
programs.why: POJK 25/2019 implements Indonesia's automatic exchange of financial account information, referring to the Common Reporting Standard for identifying reportable accounts. Onboarding and reporting staff need to collect self-certifications and report accurately.

references.title: POJK Nomor 25/POJK.03/2019 tentang Pelaporan Informasi Nasabah Asing Terkait Perpajakan kepada Negara Mitra atau Yurisdiksi Mitra (OJK Regulation 25/2019: foreign customer tax reporting)
references.note: Banks report account information on foreign tax residents for exchange with partner jurisdictions; the elucidation links the identification procedures to the Common Reporting Standard.

programs.title: Indonesia | Treasury and Trade Finance Settlement Certification (PBI 5/2024)
audience: Supervisors and executive officers in these units
programs.why: Bank Indonesia's competency standards cover the operational settlement of treasury transactions and trade financing as a payment system activity. Directors, executive officers, supervisors and staff carrying out this work must hold the matching competency-based training or competency certificate within six months of appointment and keep it current through competence maintenance at least every three years.

references.title: Peraturan Bank Indonesia Nomor 5 Tahun 2024 tentang Standardisasi Kompetensi di Bidang Sistem Pembayaran (BI Regulation 5/2024 on competency standards in the payment system field)
references.note: Treasury transaction and trade finance settlement is a covered activity; staff doing it must hold the required certificate within six months and refresh competence at least every three years.

programs.title: Indonesia | Treasury Dealer Certification and Market Code of Conduct (BI)
programs.why: Treasury dealers at banks active in the money and FX markets must hold a valid treasury certificate at the right level, follow the market code of conduct and be registered with Bank Indonesia, and banks must have internal procedures to make dealers comply. Under PADG 17/2026, staff need their certificate from the day they take up the role and the treasury director within six months; certificates last at most three years and are renewed by recertification.

references.title: Peraturan Bank Indonesia Nomor 6 Tahun 2024 tentang Pasar Uang dan Pasar Valuta Asing (BI Regulation 6/2024 on the money market and foreign exchange market)
references.note: Treasury dealers must act professionally, follow the market code of conduct and hold a treasury certificate; banks must use registered dealers, check certificates and have procedures for code compliance.

references.title: PADG Nomor 17 Tahun 2026 tentang Penguatan Kualitas Pelaku dan Penyelenggara Infrastruktur Pasar Keuangan serta Penyelenggaraan SRO di Pasar Uang dan Pasar Valuta Asing (BI Board Member Regulation 17/2026)
references.note: Sets levels 5 to 7 of the treasury certificate by role, validity of up to three years, timing of certification, and bank duties to check certificates; it replaced PADG 13/2023.

programs.title: Indonesia | Electronic Customer Verification for Digital Onboarding
programs.why: When banks onboard customers through digital services they must identify the customer and verify data and the person behind it, face to face, by electronic face-to-face meeting or non face-to-face electronic means, using at least two authentication factors and, for electronic methods, a biometric factor. Third-party verification tools must follow the AML/CFT rules on third parties. Onboarding staff need to apply these steps; no training duty is set.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 21 Tahun 2023 tentang Layanan Digital oleh Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 21/2023 on digital services by commercial banks)
references.note: Banks must identify and verify digital customers using two-factor authentication, including a biometric factor for remote methods, and may use authorised data sources and third-party tools under AML/CFT rules.

programs.title: Indonesia | AI Governance for Indonesian Banking (OJK Guideline)
programs.why: OJK's 2025 guideline on artificial intelligence governance for Indonesian banking is a non-binding reference that covers the AI lifecycle, risk management and governance. It expects banks to have staff with adequate multidisciplinary AI knowledge, to build AI competence especially in units that implement and use AI, and to train employees to understand the AI systems they use. It is good practice rather than a binding training rule.

references.title: Tata Kelola Kecerdasan Artifisial Perbankan Indonesia (OJK guideline on Artificial Intelligence Governance for Indonesian Banking)
references.note: Banks should have staff with adequate AI knowledge and experience, build AI competence in units implementing and using AI, and train employees on the AI systems they use.

notes: POJK 8/2023 (in force 14 June 2023) replaced POJK 12/POJK.01/2017 and its 2019 amendment, added proliferation financing, and turned the old periodic training duty into training at least once a year; older implementing circulars such as SEOJK 38/2017 survive only where consistent with it.

POJK 22/2023 (promulgated 22 December 2023) replaced POJK 6/POJK.07/2022 on consumer protection; POJK 38/2025 (promulgated 22 December 2025) on OJK lawsuits for consumer protection revoked Article 98(1)(b) and Articles 99 and 100 of POJK 22/2023.

PADK 1/2026 on IT operation by commercial banks took effect on 1 March 2026 and revoked SEOJK 21/SEOJK.03/2017; it adds detail on IT governance, IT service providers and personal data protection. SEOJK 29/2022 on cyber resilience remains the companion circular.

POJK 12/2024 on anti-fraud strategy took effect three months after promulgation on 31 July 2024 and replaced POJK 39/POJK.03/2019 for commercial banks, extending one integrated anti-fraud standard to all financial institutions.

POJK 24/2022 on bank staff development revoked Bank Indonesia's 2009 risk management certification regulation; SEOJK 28/2022 now governs risk management certificates, and banks must spend at least 3.5 percent of the prior year's gross salary cost on staff development.
The P2SK Law (Law 4/2023) amended the Banking Law's secrecy provisions, gave OJK market-conduct powers and requires financial sector actors to fund continuous staff education and training.

Law 27/2022 on Personal Data Protection applies to banks, but its official text could not be opened during this review because the legislation portals refused automated access; no provision is cited for it.

Payment systems: Bank Indonesia's PBI 10/2025 and PADG 32/2025 on payment system industry rules took effect on 31 March 2026 and revoked PADG 24/7/PADG/2022. PBI 5/2024 on payment system competency standards replaced PBI 21/16/PBI/2019; staff already in post had until 31 December 2026 to hold the required certificate.

Treasury: PBI 6/2024 on the money and FX markets took effect on 16 July 2024, and PADG 17/2026 (in force 30 June 2026) replaced PADG 13/2023 on treasury certification, the market code of conduct and the self-regulatory organisation for the money and FX markets.

Prudential: POJK 5/2024 extended recovery plans to all commercial banks and revoked POJK 14/POJK.03/2017; POJK 19/2024 added ILAAP to the LCR rule, with SEOJK 26/2025 phasing in reporting from December 2026; POJK 22/2025 replaced POJK 63/2020 on reporting via APOLO; PADK 10/2026 on country and transfer risk starts with June 2027 data and cites Law 4/2026 amending the P2SK Law.
